comment: THE FUNCTION-EXECUTE SURFACE, ONE SOURCE (R-2026-09-24-74 BB-2). For every function in the schemas below, which of the three client-facing roles can EXECUTE it, and why. The key is the function's identity as pg_catalog prints it with search_path set to pg_catalog: schema.name(argument types), so the types are qualified the same way on every database. Read by tests/db/authenticated_executable_closed_list.test.ts, which derives its closed list from the entries authenticated can execute in the exposed schemas, and by scripts/readback_function_grants.sh, which holds hosted to this file after an apply. tests/db/function_grants.test.ts holds the local catalogue equal to it, entry for entry. So a grant changed anywhere reds against this file, and it is changed here, with its reason, in the same change. MEASURED on the local stack on 2026-09-24 at 020: service_role holds EXECUTE on none of this repository's functions (each migration revokes it by name), and graphql_public.graphql is Supabase's own, executable by all three.

app.assert_member(uuid, app.app_role).why: 011: the membership check the SECURITY DEFINER RPCs call; never called by a client

app.assert_operator().why: 020: the operator check the operator_* functions call

app.gate(app.ward_category, app.tri_stat.why: 006: the gate rule, called by the projection

app.gate_for_facility(app.ward_category,.why: 006: the gate over a facility's duty flags, called by the projection

app.operator_session(uuid).why: 020: the session id the operator writes record in their audit rows

app.project_facility(uuid).why: 008, restated in 020: the only writer of the public mirrors

app.provision_begin(uuid, text, text).why: 020: the provisioning gates (-71 C). Only the provisioning script calls it, as the owner; executable by no client role (BB-2)

app.provision_complete(uuid, uuid).why: 020: the provisioning gates (-71 C). Only the provisioning script calls it, as the owner; executable by no client role (BB-2)

app.refresh_lga_rollup().why: 009, restated in 017 and 020: the rollup's only writer, run by pg_cron

app.regenerate_snapshot().why: 016, restated in 019: the snapshot generator, run by pg_cron

app.snapshot_retention().why: 016: how long the generator keeps snapshot rows

graphql_public.graphql(text, text, jsonb.why: Supabase-owned; the GraphQL entry point shipped with every project, not written here

public.my_facility_wards().why: 011: a ward loads its own facility's wards

public.operator_add_category(text, text,.why: 020: an operator adds a category (-71 E)

public.operator_create_facility(text, te.why: 020: an operator creates a facility (-71 E)

public.operator_edit_facility(text, inte.why: 020: an operator edits a facility (-71 E, J1)

public.operator_set_facility_listed(text.why: 020: an operator lists a facility (-71 B)

why_hosted_only: FUNCTIONS HOSTED HAS AND THIS REPOSITORY DOES NOT CREATE (R-2026-09-24-77 BE-1). Kept apart from `functions` so the two cannot blur: tests/db/function_grants.test.ts holds the LOCAL catalogue equal to `functions` and asserts no entry below exists locally, and the D3 closed list reads `functions` only. scripts/readback_function_grants.sh accepts an entry below only if EVERY recorded property matches on the database it reads -- the roles, the owner, the return type and SECURITY DEFINER -- so a change to a callable return type, a widened grant or a new owner reads STOP. An entry absent from the database it reads (as locally) is not a failure. A function in neither section is still a STOP.

public.rls_auto_enable().why: Supabase's automatic-RLS feature: the function of event trigger ensure_rls (ddl_command_end), which runs ALTER TABLE ... ENABLE (not FORCE) ROW LEVEL SECURITY on each new table in schema public. Not callable over the API: an event_trigger function cannot be called directly (Cowork's readings, 2026-09-24: PostgREST answers 400, 0A000, and api.openbed.ng answers 404). Recorded as undeclared hosted platform configuration by R-2026-09-22-55 D3 and -56 A7; it read STOP at fence 6 of 020's apply on 2026-09-24, and BE-1 ruled it here.
